questions.question:
**Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.**

She was __fined of driving__ over the speed limit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **fined for driving**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the original sentence, the word "**of**" is incorrectly used after "**fined**."
 
• The correct preposition to use with "**fined**" is "**for**".
 
• "Fine of driving" and "fined for drive" are both **incorrect **grammatically.
 
• The correct structure is "**fined for + gerund (verb+ing)**".
 
• The construction "**for + gerund" (verb + -ing form)** is a grammatical structure used to indicate the purpose, reason, or cause for action. 
 
• When someone is fined, it means they are being penalized or required to pay a certain amount of money as a consequence of their actions. In this case, the action is "driving over the speed limit."

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Corrected sentence:** *She was fined for driving over the speed limit.*

questions.question:
**Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.**

In humans, consumption of alcohol stimulate brain cells to release mood-altering dopamine.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: "**stimulate brain cells to**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error here lies in the **Subject-Verb agreement**.
 
• Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or both plural. 
 
• A singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
 
• The verb "**stimulate**" should be in the singular form "**stimulates**" to agree with the singular subject "**consumption**."
 
• There are no more mistakes in the remaining alternatives.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**The corrected sentence would be:** *In humans, consumption of alcohol stimulates brain cells to release mood-altering dopamine.*

questions.question:

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.solution:

• The sentence is in the present continuous tense, indicating a future event.
 
• The verb "**look forward to**" is followed by a **gerund **(verb + ing).
 
• "**Meeting**" is the correct gerund form of the verb "meet."
 
• In the context of the statement, the gerund "**meeting**" takes on the role of the object of the preposition "**to**."
 
• It indicates the action that the speaker is looking forward to.
 
• Gerunds are commonly used in this way to express actions that serve as the focus or purpose of an action or event.
 
• The sentence means the speaker is excited to see the listener at their favourite restaurant in the future.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Complete sentence:** *I am looking forward to meeting __you at our favourite restaurant.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Drastic times call for drastic measures

options.text: When you are extremely desperate you need to take extremely desperate actions
Don't rely on it until you sure of it
Something that ends at the last minute or last few seconds
Do not pull all your resources in one possibility

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **When you are extremely desperate you need to take extremely desperate actions**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**drastic times call for drastic measures**" means that in a situation of extreme difficulty or crisis, one must take extreme actions to solve the problem. (अत्यधिक कठिनाई या संकट की स्थिति में, समस्या को हल करने के लिए व्यक्ति को अत्यधिक कार्रवाई करनी चाहिए)

 
 
• **For example- ***When the prolonged recession forced him to shut down his business, Dev decided to sell groceries to make ends meet. Drastic times call for drastic measures!*

 
 
 
 
• The word "**drastic**" means extreme or severe, and "**measures**" refer to actions taken to solve a problem.
 
• This idiom emphasizes the urgency of the situation and the need for immediate action.
 
• It suggests that the usual or conventional methods may not work in such situations, and one needs to be creative and bold in finding a solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Let us look at the other options.

 
• Option 2: "**Don't rely on it until you sure of it**" is not related to the idiom and is a general advice to be cautious before trusting something or someone.
 
• Option 3: "**Something that ends at the last minute or last few seconds**" is not related to the idiom and describes a situation of last-minute or sudden completion.
 
• Option 4: "**Do not pull all your resources in one possibility**" is not related to the idiom and advises against putting all efforts or resources in one option or possibility.
